subject: Archaeology
title: The First Beer Brewers
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The First Beer Brewers.

hook.text: Mesopotamians invented beer at least 5,000 years ago. Workers were paid in beer rations — about two liters per day.

buildup.text: The oldest known beer recipe is on a Sumerian tablet from 1800 BCE. It describes a thick, bread-based brew.

discovery.text: Archaeologists found chemical traces of barley beer in jars at Godin Tepe in Iran dating to 3400 BCE.

twist.text: Some scholars think beer, not bread, motivated the invention of agriculture. Growing grain for beer came first.

climax.text: The goddess Ninkasi was the divine brewer. A hymn to her is also a step-by-step brewing recipe — the oldest how-to.

punchline.text: Civilization may have started because someone wanted a drink.

quiz.question: What provocative theory do some scholars hold about beer and farming?
options: Beer was used as medicine long before it became a beverage
Growing grain for beer may have motivated the invention of agriculture
Beer was invented independently on every continent at the same time
